newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares close at record but off intraday peak.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares close at record but off intraday peak.

text.p: Dutch shares closed at a new record on Wednesday after earlier setting a fresh all-time peak as the market celebrated the Federal Reserve's decision on Tuesday to leave U.S. interest rates unchanged.
"It's pretty clear that the market was relieved by the 'rate hike that never was'," one dealer said. "That frees us from immediate interest rate worries until July."
The AEX index of leading shares closed up 16.48 points, 2.09 percent, at 803.93 after hitting all-time-high of 806.01 in the midsession.

The AEX took out tough resistance at the 800 point level early, aided by position covering on the options exchange, and the close above this augured well for an extension of the index's advance, dealers said.
But the market would quickly fall back into a familiar pattern of second-guessing economic data ahead of the next FOMC meeting, some cautioned.

"The outlook for the short-term is positive, but we are again going to be living from number to number in the U.S.," one analyst said, though he emphasized that the Dutch market's relative performance had been good.
"The AEX is doing really well. When Wall Street drops we are not following all the way. When it rises we are turbocharged."
The positive mood was reflected among the major stocks, with 29 advances o the AEX and just one decline.
Financial group ING was a major gainer ending up almost six percent, buoyed by new details of its profitability, brokers said.
The shares closed up 4.70 at 84.80 guilders, after earlier touching a recor high of 85.30.

The group on Tuesday issued a prospectus for its New York listing next month, showing that 1996 net profit was 1.35 billion guilders higher under U.S GAAP accounting methods than under the Dutch equivalent.
"It gives (investors) a different view on the stock," said one dealer.

Bank ABN AMRO also generated interest linked to its New York listing, whic went through on Wednesday. ABN topped the volume list with nearly three times as much turnover as the next most active stock.
Its New York shares started trading on Wednesday right on their resale price of $18.50 per share.
Airline KLM shrugged off poor 1996/97 year results to end up 1.60 guilders at 59.80.
Analysts attributed the positive reaction partly to a change in top management with CEO Pieter Bouw announcing his intention to resign in August.
Net profit at the Dutch flag carrier for 1996/97 fell to 236 million guilders ($125.2 million) from 547 million.
This included a pre-tax provision of 290 million for the Focus 2000 restructuring programme which aims to boost operating income by 1.5 billion guilders over the next three years.

Among the smallcaps, transport firm Hes Beheer jumped 1.40 guilders, or 11.76 percent, to 13.30 on news of a one-for-one rights issue. Hes said the solvency of the group would increase substantially as a result of the issue.
